::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 2nd 1896  
**From:** Elderfield  Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear[Mr Holgate](people/person_1643.qmd)
This is really only an abridgement of the [article](cmy_books/cmybook_66.qmd) in the Christian Remembrancer, except that I added the going to Winchester College chapel in 1854. I signed the paper because once or twice I found myself writing <u>I</u> to a personal reminiscence, but it can be altered if you wish it.[^1] I think [Lord Seaton](people/person_313.qmd)’s personal appearance is fully described in the paper. He was the most striking old man I ever saw. The best likeness of him is one of [Richmond](people/person_1731.qmd)’s Crayons. I have an engraving of it, I think the original is at [Beechwood](organizations/other_126.qmd), but I am not sure. There is another print that I do not like so much, and a full length picture which I believe was done for the United Services Club. There is a print from that but I do not like it - it is in Life Guards uniform and that being cavalry - is apt to look awkward on an infantry man. There is another small portrait of him at [Puslinch](organizations/other_123.qmd), a much younger man - but I never realized it, never having known him till his return from Canada.

My [mother](people/person_1606.qmd) was [his step father](people/person_106.qmd)’s youngest daughter, my [father](people/person_1631.qmd) was in his regiment, and was first cousin to his [wife](people/person_314.qmd).

Anything about the pictures might best be learnt from [the present Lord Seaton](people/person_318.qmd), Beechwood Plympton

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: This letter, and the preceding one to Holgate, evidently relate to an untraced article by CMY on Lord Seaton.
